title: Charity
coreMove: Evaluate giving as help plus public signal, then ask whether visibility is serving impact or the giver.
sourcePressure: The source argues that charity often signals wealth, empathy, and prosocial orientation, so giving patterns can fit social display better than pure effectiveness.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The writer turns charity into hypocrisy or effective-altruism math and loses mixed motives.

sourceAnchors.name: charity signaling wealth
sourceAnchors.detail: The source says charity can signal wealth.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: A gift can show surplus even while it funds something real.

sourceAnchors.name: charity signaling empathy and prosocial orientation
sourceAnchors.detail: The source says giving can signal empathy and prosocial orientation.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The donation says I care, and also asks to be read as the kind of person who cares.

sourceAnchors.name: giving patterns fitting social-display motives
sourceAnchors.detail: The source says giving patterns can fit social-display motives more than pure effectiveness.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: When the visible gift wins over the effective one, the audience has entered the budget.

exampleSpecs.domain: local food bank donor wall redesign
exampleSpecs.audience: a director balancing recognition with useful giving
exampleSpecs.stakes: public recognition may increase donations while steering gifts toward display
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Sophie moves the donor wall beside the volunteer packing line and tests whether recognition increases staples instead of only naming-rights gifts.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Canned beans rattle in crates under an unfinished donor wall.

exampleSpecs.audience: an HR lead deciding whether leaderboards help or distort
exampleSpecs.stakes: employees may give to be seen rather than to match need
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: "Teams with full participation get a badge," Luca says, and Astrid asks what happens to private hardship funds that cannot be displayed.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "Teams with full participation get a badge," Luca says beside the campaign dashboard.

exampleSpecs.audience: a coordinator redirecting visible generosity toward requested sizes
exampleSpecs.stakes: people donate impressive coats while children need plain waterproof sizes
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Javier sorts the glossy adult coats away from the children's waterproof-size list and changes the public ask to make usefulness visible.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Wet wool smell rises from the donated coats by the gym door.

exampleSpecs.audience: a couple choosing between a public registry and anonymous direct aid
exampleSpecs.stakes: guests may need a visible ritual to participate
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You have Ada add a plain impact note beside each public gift option so display pulls money toward actual need instead of away from it.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You see the registry page before the envelopes are addressed.

exampleSpecs.audience: a principal checking what the prize ladder teaches
exampleSpecs.stakes: children learn that giving counts most when ranked
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: What happens when empathy comes with a gold-level lanyard?
exampleSpecs.firstImage: What does the lanyard teach before the cause is named?

exampleSpecs.audience: a board member measuring response to named stories versus unglamorous repairs
exampleSpecs.stakes: visible empathy may ignore invisible infrastructure
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: It took Patrick one flooded kennel to see that the public loved rescue photos but skipped drainage work, so he pairs every story with the hidden repair it requires.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: It took Patrick one flooded kennel to reread the appeal photos.

skillTargets: separate charitable impact from signal value
identify wealth, empathy, and prosocial signals in giving
design giving prompts that use visibility without letting display dominate

tryThisNowSpec: Before your next donation or favor, write what it helps and what it signals. Change one detail so the help stays first.
